Turn a photo into SVG art

Your photo, reimagined as shapes

A photograph contains many subtle tones and textures. A vector trace reduces those pixels into colored shapes, giving you a bold illustration-like interpretation that can scale.

The number of colors and amount of detail change the style and complexity. Fewer colors create a simpler, poster-like look. More colors can keep extra nuance but may make the file harder to edit.

Open the free SVG tool ↗

How to make a vector from a photo

Upload a JPG, PNG, or WebP photo. Choose a palette and detail setting, generate the SVG, and compare the result. Adjust settings and try again to explore a different look.

Will it look exactly like the original photo?

No. SVG shapes cannot reproduce all photographic texture exactly. The result is a stylized approximation whose look depends on the photo, palette, and detail setting.

What kind of photo should I start with?

Clear subjects and good contrast often make a more readable trace. Try different color counts to find a useful balance between recognizable detail and a clean graphic.
